doc.title: Date Class
doc.para:
Date Class Although the features to create a Date object from a string and to create a string from an object are not implemented, it is otherwise mostly compatible with JavaScript's Date.
The constructor syntax is as follows:
new Date(); new Date(<date string>); new Date(<year>, <month(0...)=0>, <day=1>, <hour=0>, <minute=0>, <second=0>);
The first syntax requires no arguments. In this case, it holds the current date and time at the moment the constructor is executed. The second syntax specifies a date string. The date string must be specified in one of the following formats: ANSI C asctime() format, defined in RFC1123, defined in RFC1036, or "year/month/day hour:minute:second" format. Date strings are recognized automatically, and while variations in format are supported to some extent, strings that differ significantly from the expected format may not be recognized. The third syntax specifies the year, month, day, hour, minute, and second.
Implemented methods (JavaScript compatible) : setYear/getYear (Set/get the 4-digit AD year in local time) setMonth/getMonth (Set/get the month in local time) setDate/getDate (Set/get the day of the month in local time) setHours/getHours (Set/get the hour in local time) setMinutes/getMinutes (Set/get the minute in local time) setSeconds/getSeconds (Set/get the second in local time) setTime/getTime (Set/get the elapsed milliseconds since January 1, 1970 0:00) getDay (Get the day of the week) parse (Parse a date string)
